description: Manually inspectable cases for the Phase 4 LLM adjudication layer. Run with: python main.py --live-llm-test. The 'what_to_check' notes guide a human reviewer. They are never read by the analysis code and do not influence any verdict.

cases.text: I saw the man with the telescope.
cases.what_to_check: Phase 2 flags a PP-attachment candidate. Both readings are ordinary English, so a genuine ambiguity with two distinct interpretations is the expected outcome.

cases.text: I deposited money at the bank.
cases.what_to_check: Phase 3 ranks the financial sense first but with a small margin. Also check the syntactic 'at the bank' candidate: an ordinary reader attaches it to 'deposited', so it is a candidate the LLM should be free to reject.

cases.text: The fisherman sat on the bank of the river.
cases.what_to_check: The phrase 'of the river' fixes the meaning of 'bank' inside the sentence itself. Check whether the lexical candidate is judged not ambiguous.

cases.text: John told David that he was late.
cases.what_to_check: Phase 2 finds two antecedents for 'he'. Both are natural readings.

cases.text: The chicken is ready to eat.
cases.what_to_check: The textbook agent/patient ambiguity. Also check the lexical candidates on 'chicken' and 'eat', which the rule-based layer over-flags.

cases.text: She bought three apples at the market.
cases.what_to_check: Phase 2 flags PP attachment because '[the apples at the market]' is structurally available. An ordinary reader takes one reading only. Check whether the LLM rejects the structural candidate.

cases.text: The crane lifted the heavy container.
cases.what_to_check: Phase 3 ranks the BIRD sense first with a margin large enough to count as resolved - a documented failure. Check whether the LLM selects the machine sense instead; if it does, the application derives agrees_with_phase3 = false by comparing sense keys (the LLM does not report agreement).
